title: The audit sealer chains only by a `tenant_id` column, so an object whose organization lives in another column cannot be sealed
body:
repo:cloud#3 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbZqfEd7pcckjz3pGqn

Filing gate: ② a framework seam that a cloud card is blocked on (objectstack-ai/cloud#4128, Enterprise audit tamper-evidence stage 2). The cloud lane files this card and leaves first touch (domain, queue) to triage. Drafted by the cloud#4128 card thread; every file:line was read at objectstack `b914e72` (cloud's pin, 18.5.0).
Dedupe: `org:objectstack-ai is:issue` with this card's dedupe words → 0 hits.

**Business reason.** cloud#4128 item 4 opts Enterprise's AI audit trail (`sys_ai_audit_log`) into tamper evidence, as ADR-0154 D10 says it will ("Enterprise's `sys_ai_audit_log` opts in from cloud", ADR line 144). A financial customer's reviewer asks the same proof of the AI tool-call trail as of the main audit log. Today that object cannot be sealed at all.

**What happens at the pin.**
- `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/sealer.ts:332-334`: `plans()` refuses any object declaring `lifecycle.seal` that has no `tenant_id` field ("it declares no 'tenant_id' field, so its rows cannot be chained per organization") and reports it at error. The object is then never sealed.
- The chain is read from `tenant_id` only: `sealer.ts:220` (`tenantOf`), `verifier.ts:253` (`tenantOf`), and the signed body's member `tenant_id` (`signed-body.ts:65`, `:290`, `:331`).
- `sys_ai_audit_log` has no `tenant_id`. Its organization is the `organization_id` column the registry injects (ADR-0131), which cloud's interceptor relies on (cloud `packages/security-enterprise/src/ai-governance/tool-interceptor.ts:149`). The cloud design that ADR-0154 was drafted from names exactly that column as the chain key: "per organization (`sys_audit_log.tenant_id`, `sys_ai_audit_log.organization_id`)" (cloud `docs/design/audit-tamper-evidence.md:118-119`).

**What cloud needs.** A sealed object can name the column its rows are chained by (for example `lifecycle.seal.chainField`, default `tenant_id`), read by the sealer, the verifier and the proof bundle, with the signed body keeping its `tenant_id` member as the chain's organization id. A spec key is a metadata-protocol change, so the shape is the framework's to decide. Cloud will not add a duplicate `tenant_id` column to `sys_ai_audit_log` as a workaround.

**Also needed before cloud can use it (cloud side, not this card):** cloud#4129 (retention for `sys_ai_audit_log`, ruled A). `lifecycle.class: 'audit'` requires a bounding policy (`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`, the superRefine after `seal`), and `seal` is for class `audit` only.

**Done when.** On a real kernel, an object whose organization is in `organization_id` and which declares `lifecycle.seal` with that column seals one chain per organization, and `os audit verify --org X` reports its rows.

**Cloud consumer.** objectstack-ai/cloud#4128 (item 4).
Dedupe words: `audit sealer chain column`, `lifecycle.seal tenant_id`, `sealed object organization_id`.
